channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Pointed! Bloomberg’s Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
item.description: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg’s Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and David Gura as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Entrepreneurs Behind Poppi Start Over
item.description: Poppi founders Allison and Stephen Ellsworth tell Bloomberg This Weekend how they turned a farmers market business into a nearly $2 billion beverage brand and what they learned from the decade-long journey. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, the couple explains why they are starting over with Jetty, a new hydration brand, and how lessons about social media, hiring and building a team are shaping their second act. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How China’s Intelligence Operations Target Tech
item.description: Former CIA counterintelligence analyst Peter Mattis tells Bloomberg This Weekend how China’s Ministry of State Security can use business and personal relationships to gather intelligence and potentially influence decision-making in strategically important industries. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Mattis explains why technology executives can become valuable targets even without access to classified information and how AI is expanding the capabilities of Chinese intelligence operations. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed’s Collins Says ‘Steady, Gradual’ Rate Hikes Appropriate
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins said a gradual path for interest-rate hikes will be appropriate to lower inflation, as the labor market gains solid footing without adding to price pressures.
item.dc:creator: Maria Eloisa Capurro

item.title: The Stadium Bidding War Shaking Up the Midwest
item.description: The Chicago Bears are weighing three possible homes for a new stadium: downtown Chicago, suburban Arlington Heights and Hammond, Indiana. The competition has turned into a high-stakes economic development battle involving billions of dollars in potential investment, tax incentives and public financing. Supporters say a new stadium could generate jobs, development and tax revenue, but former Indiana Governor Mitch Daniels warns that emotion can push politicians into deals that leave taxpayers paying the bill long after the ribbon cutting. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SpaceX Pushes Starship Reusability to New Test
item.description: Space Network co-founder Ross Hamilton tells Bloomberg This Weekend why SpaceX’s attempt to catch Starship after its return from orbit could mark a major step toward making the rocket system fully reusable. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Hamilton explains how more frequent and less expensive launches could accelerate Starlink expansion, orbital data centers and SpaceX’s broader ambitions in space. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent, Lutnick Clash Over Nvidia China Curbs
item.description: Axios AI policy reporter Maria Curi tells Bloomberg This Weekend about tensions inside the Trump administration over efforts to restrict the flow of advanced Nvidia chips to China and scrutiny of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s handling of Megaspeed. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Curi explains the reported disagreements between Lutnick and other senior officials, including Scott Bessent, and the national security questions surrounding US technology exports to China. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Heads to China for Talks With Xi and Putin
item.description: Bloomberg White House correspondent Jeff Mason tells Bloomberg This Weekend how the Trump administration responded to a nationwide FAA ground stop and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy’s push for $50 billion to modernize the US air traffic control system. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Mason also looks ahead to President Donald Trump’s Asia trip and a planned meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping as technology and AI remain in focus. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SpaceX’s S&P 500 Bid Gets New Life as Musk Pitches Tesla Merger
item.description: Just months after SpaceX was denied a swift entry into the S&P 500 Index, Elon Musk may have found a backdoor: Merging with Tesla Inc., one of the stock-market benchmark’s biggest members.
item.dc:creator: Jordan Fitzgerald and Lu Wang

item.title: David Cameron Sees Hope in Alzheimer’s Research
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, former UK Prime Minister David Cameron discusses the personal toll of losing his mother to Alzheimer’s and the accelerating search for better diagnostics, treatments and ultimately a cure. Cameron tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini about promising drug research, the potential of blood tests to transform diagnosis and why governments should move faster to support clinical trials and expand access to new treatments. Cameron’s Ending Alzheimer’s podcast launches November 16. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ukraine Peace Push Turns to NATO and Donbas
item.description: Bloomberg Economics defense lead Becca Wasser tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a US proposal linking NATO membership to Ukrainian concessions in the Donbas represents movement in peace talks but faces significant political and security hurdles. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Wasser also examines Ukraine’s battlefield pressures and how the US could reshape its military presence in the Middle East after the war with Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Miller’s White House Ascent Rattles Mexico Trade Negotiators
item.description: A new and not-so-friendly face is poised to loom over the negotiating table where the US and Mexico are still trying to hammer out a trade deal.
item.dc:creator: Gonzalo Soto

item.title: Air Travel Chaos Puts FAA Systems in Focus
item.description: Bloomberg Intelligence senior airlines analyst George Ferguson tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the nationwide ground stop underscores the difficulty of modernizing an aging US air traffic control system while keeping flights moving safely. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ferguson explains why upgrading legacy technology is so complicated and how airlines face the challenge of restoring schedules after thousands of cancellations and delays. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Guinea Plans Bauxite Index as It Seeks to Bolster Ore Prices
item.description: Guinea, the world’s biggest exporter of bauxite, plans to establish an index for the raw material as part of wider efforts to bolster prices.
item.dc:creator: Ougna Camara

item.title: Goldman Sachs Sees 19% Return on Asia ex-Japan Stocks in 2027
item.description: Goldman Sachs expects earnings growth to drive a 19% return for the MSCI Asia ex-Japan Index in dollar terms next year, even as it warned that uncertainty over artificial intelligence could fuel volatility.
item.dc:creator: Echo Wong

item.title: How Wall Street Is Bracing For the Post-Jensen Huang Nvidia Era
item.description: The ultimate key man risk.
item.dc:creator: Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway

item.title: Odd Lots: Wall Street and the Post-Huang Nvidia Era (Podcast)
item.description: Nvidia's post-Jensen Huang era has just begun and there are so many open questions about the company's future. Who will the board choose to be Nvidia's next CEO? Will the government crack down on the chipmaker's business practices, particularly in Asia? And will Nvidia's uncertain position begin to spillover into the wider AI ecosystem, from the labs to data center providers? Stacy Rasgon, managing director and senior analyst at Bernstein, isn't optimistic about the short term future of Nvidia a
item.dc:creator: Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway

item.title: The Oil Market Is Brimming With Crude Despite Tanker Attacks
item.description: More than eight months into the Iran war, smoke continues to billow from oil tankers as Tehran presses ahead with repeated attacks near the Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Alex Longley, Anthony Di Paola, Shariq Khan and Mia Gindis

item.title: Centrica, Equinor in Next Round of Germany’s Uniper Sale
item.description: Centrica Plc and Equinor ASA are among companies advancing to the second round of the sale process for Germany’s Uniper SE, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Eyk Henning and Eva Brendel

item.title: Trading Firm IMC Plans to Double Staff in Hong Kong
item.description: IMC Trading expects to roughly double headcount in its Hong Kong office over the next two years, the latest sign of a rush among foreign firms to expand in the city.
item.dc:creator: Bei Hu
